topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the students to the final lecture and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the implementation, mechanisms of action, and clinical limitations of conventional non-targeted cancer treatments.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic vulnerabilities and genetic defects in cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific genetic, checkpoint, and metabolic vulnerabilities unique to cancer cells can be exploited for targeted therapeutic intervention.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and kinase inhibitor therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the therapeutic targeting of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases, detailing inhibitor mechanisms, resistance pathways, and clinical management strategies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how engineered monoclonal antibodies can be used to target tumor surface markers either for direct cell killing or for delivering cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the principles and clinical technologies used to harness and genetically engineer the host immune system to destroy tumor cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine broader systemic hurdles, historical survival progress, ethical considerations, and evolving paradigms in the future of cancer therapy.
